Report Description
THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE COMMAND CENTER VIA THIRD PARTY IN REFERENCE TO A HIGH LEVEL RELEASE OF RADIOACTIVE TRITIUM THAT WAS DETECTED BELOW SNOW AND ICE HANGING FROM A BUILDING DURING ROUTINE SAMPLING ON THURSDAY. ***REPORT PROVIDED ON FRIDAY, MARCH 06, 2015*** THE LATEST COLD SNAP HAS DELIVERED A TROUBLING SURPRISE AT PSEG NUCLEAR"S SALEM/HOPE CREEK REACTOR COMPLEX: THE DISCOVERY OF RADIOACTIVE TRITIUM IN SNOW AND ICE OUTSIDE A HOPE CREEK BUILDING AT LEVELS 500 TIMES HIGHER THAN FEDERAL WATER QUALITY STANDARDS. IT WAS REPORTED THAT AN ESTIMATED 10 MILLION PICOCURIES PER LITER OF TRITIUM WAS DISCOVERED IN A CONFINED AREA, IT WAS THE SECOND-HIGHEST CONCENTRATION REPORTED IN ANY TRITIUM LEAK AND POLLUTION INCIDENT NATIONWIDE. THE FEDERAL DRINKING WATER LIMIT FOR TRITIUM, AN ISOTOPE OF HYDROGEN, IS 20,000 PICOCURIES PER LITER.

WINDS WERE FROM THE SOUTHWEST AT 10 KTS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE. UNCERTAINTIES: THE SHAPE OF THE SLICK DOES APPEAR TO BE A LITTLE WISPY IN SHAPE ON THE EDGES, AND THERE ARE NO SHARP TURNS.
